findings.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching live buffer keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration or dual-read support makes rolling deploys fail with WRONGTYPE and can stall span ingestion and flushing until old keys expire.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:58 — No test inserts more than 1,000 differently timed spans, so oldest-first eviction and retention of the triggering span are unverified.

goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching live buffer keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration or dual-read support makes rolling deploys fail with WRONGTYPE and can stall span ingestion and flushing until old keys expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear change from Redis set commands (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to sorted set commands (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. During a rolling deployment, old code instances will use set commands while new instances use sorted set commands on the same Redis keys. Redis will return WRONGTYPE errors when a set command is executed on a sorted set key or vice versa. There's no migration strategy, dual-read support, or key versioning visible in the diff to handle this transition safely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 silently attaches deeper span chains to the wrong segment and can fragment or lose traces under adversarially deep input.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the loop limit in add-buffer.lua being reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 (line 30). The original comment explicitly states 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1,000, span chains deeper than 1,000 levels will now fail to be properly joined. The loop traverses redirect chains to find the correct set_span_id, and if it terminates early due to the lower limit, spans will be attached to incorrect segments. This is a correctness bug that could cause trace fragmentation for deep span hierarchies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — A caller-controlled negative optimized cursor reaches Django queryset negative slicing, which raises an assertion and lets authorized callers reliably turn audit-log requests into 500 responses.
matched_golden_ids: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same problem as the golden comment - both are about OptimizedCursorPaginator's handling of negative cursor.offset values being passed directly to queryset slicing. The candidate specifically mentions line 877 in the paginator, negative cursor values reaching Django queryset slicing, and the resulting assertion error. This is the same underlying issue about negative offsets being improperly handled in the get_result() method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 — Requiring end_timestamp_precise without rollout fallback makes any legacy or partially upgraded producer payload raise KeyError and repeatedly fail the entire consumer batch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in factory.py line 141, the code accesses val['end_timestamp_precise'] directly without using .get() with a default value. This is a required field access that will raise KeyError if the field is missing. Looking at the cast to SpanEvent type and the direct dictionary access pattern, if any producer sends messages without this field (legacy producers, partial rollouts, or schema version mismatches), the consumer will fail. The finding correctly identifies this as a potential issue - the code should use val.get('end_timestamp_precise', some_default) for backward compatibility during rollout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79 — The opt-in public API path replaces DateTimePaginator with a numeric paginator, so datetime rows cannot produce cursors and authorized requests fail instead of preserving the endpoint contract.
src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Writing sorted sets into keys that may still contain pre-deploy Redis sets raises WRONGTYPE and drops whole in-flight batches during rollout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis sets (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to sorted sets (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py. During deployment rollout, some Redis keys may still contain data stored as sets from the old code, while new code tries to use sorted set commands (zadd at line 197). Redis will return WRONGTYPE error when sorted set commands are used on keys containing regular sets. This is a real deployment/migration issue that could cause data loss during the transition period.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — Optimized pagination is used for a datetime field but math.floor/math.ceil cannot accept datetime values, so every nonempty optimized audit-log page fails.
matched_golden_ids: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the OptimizedCursorPaginator's get_item_key method uses math.floor/math.ceil on datetime values, which causes a TypeError. Both comments point to the same bug - that floor/ceil cannot accept datetime values when the order_by field is a datetime field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — Passing a negative cursor offset reaches a negative Django QuerySet slice, which Django rejects instead of handling as claimed.
matched_golden_ids: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment. Both are about negative cursor offset values being passed to Django QuerySet slicing. The golden comment specifically mentions that in BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, start_offset = offset is set without clamping, allowing negative offset values. The candidate issue points to the same file (src/sentry/api/paginator.py) and describes the same problem - negative cursor offset reaching negative Django QuerySet slice. The candidate even notes that Django rejects this instead of handling it properly, which is the consequence of the unclamped negative offset issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 silently splits span trees deeper than 1,001 levels into the wrong segment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the loop limit being reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 at line 30. The original comment stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1,000, the same limitation now applies at a lower threshold. However, this is not necessarily a 'bug' - it appears to be an intentional design decision to limit resource usage (the same commit also adds span count limits of 1,000 via zpopmin). The finding correctly identifies a behavioral change, but whether trees deeper than 1,000 levels are realistic in practice is a design/architecture concern rather than a defect. The change is intentional but may have implications for edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates nearly all of BasePaginator.get_result, creating a second pagination implementation that will drift when shared cursor behavior changes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912) duplicates most of the logic from BasePaginator.get_result. Looking at the diff, the new class copies the entire pagination flow including cursor handling, offset calculation, result fetching, and cursor building. This is a legitimate architectural concern - when BasePaginator.get_result is modified, OptimizedCursorPaginator won't automatically receive those changes, leading to maintenance burden and potential drift. This is a real, specific, diff-grounded concern about code duplication that could cause future bugs, though it's not a bug itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:196 — Bulk ZADD occurs before the eviction script, so a large or interrupted batch can leave the Redis buffer above the intended 1,000-span memory bound until TTL expiry.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in buffer.py line 196, `p.zadd()` is called to add spans to Redis before the Lua script (add-buffer.lua) runs. The Lua script contains the eviction logic (`zpopmin` when span_count > 1000) at lines 55-57. However, the Python code in buffer.py performs a bulk ZADD operation in a pipeline that executes before the Lua script's eviction logic runs. This means if a large batch is added via ZADD, the 1000-span limit enforced by the Lua script won't apply to that batch until the next Lua script execution. This is a real race condition/ordering issue where the buffer can exceed the intended 1000-span limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:58 — No test inserts more than 1,000 differently timed spans, so oldest-first eviction and retention of the triggering span are unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in add-buffer.lua (lines 55-58) that evicts oldest spans when count exceeds 1000 using zpopmin. Looking at the test files in the diff, none of the test cases add more than a handful of spans (typically 4-6 spans per test). The finding correctly identifies that this new eviction behavior is untested - there's no test that verifies: 1) the 1000 span limit triggers correctly, 2) zpopmin removes the oldest spans (lowest scores), 3) the triggering span is retained. This is a legitimate missing test concern for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:44 — No rolling-deployment test covers legacy Redis set keys, which will make the new ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE path fail with WRONGTYPE until old keys expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET commands (scard, sunionstore, sadd) to SORTED SET commands (zcard, zunionstore, zadd). In buffer.py, the code changes from p.sadd() to p.zadd(), and in add-buffer.lua, the code changes from scard/sunionstore to zcard/zunionstore. During a rolling deployment, old code may have written SET keys that still exist in Redis. When new code tries to execute ZCARD or ZUNIONSTORE on these existing SET keys, Redis will return a WRONGTYPE error because you cannot use sorted set commands on regular set data types. The finding correctly identifies this as a deployment compatibility issue that would cause failures until old keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876 — No test exercises an advanced negative-offset request, so Django queryset rejection of negative slicing can ship as an administrator-visible 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces OptimizedCursorPaginator with code at lines 883-887 that explicitly allows negative offsets when enable_advanced_features is True: `start_offset = cursor.offset` (allowing negative values) followed by `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError. The finding correctly identifies that no test exercises this code path with a negative offset, meaning this bug could ship and cause 500 errors for administrators using the optimized_pagination parameter.
